$comment: Panel manifest for figures/landscape/.
Every entry names one panel: the per-figure R script that draws it, the one
PDF it writes, its page size and its seed. A figure script draws every panel
of its figure, and each panel reads its own output path, page size and seed
from here, so renumbering a panel is an edit to this file and nowhere else.
Every path in this file is relative to figures/landscape/, which the
environment variable LANDSCAPE_ROOT names (config/landscape.env).
Some figure scripts additionally write a supplementary sub-table — the one
whose numbers are that panel's numbers. That is still one computation and one
file; see co_generated_tables below and config/table_map.json.
co_generated_tables names the supplementary sub-tables THIS PANEL'S FIGURE
SCRIPT also writes, in the same run, from the same objects — see
config/table_map.json, which records the same relation from the other side.
One file, one computation, so the figure and its table cannot disagree and
nothing is computed twice.
displays_tables is the weaker relation: this panel PLOTS the numbers that
sub-table tabulates, whether or not the two were ever computed together.
not_built, on a figure, lists the panels of it this repo does not draw: what
each one is and what made it. They have no entry under panels and nothing
builds them; the figure script named there says so and stops.
Consumed by lib/panel_export.R, which every figure script sources.

panels.title: Genetic ancestry PCA, MoTrPAC participants projected onto 1000 Genomes
panels.reproducibility_note: Deterministic given its inputs, and it computes no principal component: the variant calling, the merge with 1000 Genomes, the LD pruning and the snpgdsPCA all ran once outside any pipeline and this panel consumes the result. What fixes the figure is therefore which copy of that result is read, not an RNG seed - the LD-pruning seed lives in the workflow that produced it. Under ED1A_PC_SOURCE=data_hub (the default) the participants' coordinates are the released ones from the analysis collection's resources/ prefix, pinned to a collection version in ED1.R; the 1000 Genomes reference cloud still comes from the cached RDS, because the release publishes no coordinate for a reference sample.

The numbers themselves came from the VCF workflow described below; this is that workflow's published output, and reading it is what removes the need to hold or re-run the workflow.
